title: Enterprise intake: rapid journey map + scope-prototype for Sales/CS feature bundles
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Create a lightweight, repeatable process and artifact set for aggregating enterprise feature requests from Sales/CS, producing a rapid journey-style mapping of customer pain, a hypothesis-driven scope prototype, and a quantitative first-pass priority score. Goal is to reduce noisy one-off ask handling, surface bundling opportunities across accounts, and hand a pragmatic scoping packet to Engineering (MVP spec + estimated effort band).
background: Sales and CS are currently sending dozens of account-specific feature asks to PMs/Eng that require significant back-and-forth. This causes long lead times, context loss, and inconsistent prioritization. Related playbooks exist but are inconsistently applied. We need a concise, reproducible intake that produces: (1) a canonical summary for each bundle, (2) a hypothesis map linking customer pain to business/econ impact, (3) a first-pass complexity/effort band, and (4) a priority score calibrated to Redwood's production economics thesis.
goals: Design a 1-page intake template for Sales/CS that forces problem, success metrics, and constraints
Define a 4-field scoring rubric (impact, reuse potential, strategic fit, implementation risk) and calibrate it with 6 example asks
Produce an internal scope-prototype artifact (MVP acceptance criteria + non-goals + rough effort band: Small/Medium/Large)
Pilot the flow with two Sales AE teams and one Customer Success team within 3 weeks
Integrate an output link into our problem-tracking board for handoff to Eng with clear next steps
out_of_scope: Detailed engineering design (this ticket stops at initial scoping and effort banding)
Full UX mockups beyond a 1-page wire sketch
acceptance_criteria: Intake template created and published to Drive/Confluence
Scoring rubric documented and applied to 6 historical asks with results recorded
Pilot submissions received from at least 3 unique enterprise accounts
Engineering feedback collected and a single engineer signs off on the scope packet format
Handoff checklist established and rolled into intake form (owner, expected SLA for follow-ups)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Risk: Over-baking the intake will discourage Sales from using it. Trade-off: keep the form short (3-5 fields) and provide an optional 'attachments' section for deeper context.
Risk: Scoring rubric may bias toward low-effort features. Mitigation: include a reuse/multiplicity weight to reward cross-account value.
Trade-off: Quick effort bands (S/M/L) are blunt; acceptance criteria must include a rapid engineering validation step before full scoping
implementation_notes: Propose a two-step flow: (A) Sales fills 1-page intake (problem, account list, success metric, ask provenance + required timeline), (B) PM runs a 30-minute rapid scoping session with Eng to assign effort band and finalize priority score. Create a templated Confluence page for the scope-prototype that engineers can copy into PRD templates.
deliverables: Confluence: Decision log + scoring rubric page
Spreadsheet: example scoring calibration for 6 historical asks
